newsitem.title: INDIA: Sunflower oil imports to spur Indian refineries.
newsitem.headline: Sunflower oil imports to spur Indian refineries.

text.p: Steady arrivals of sunflower oil from Argentina and the United States are expected to spur activity at Indian refineries running on idle capacity, traders and analysts said on Wednesday.
They said India's sunflower oil imports had risen after Malaysian palm olein prices shot up due to increased demand from China and Pakistan.
"Sunflower oil imports are picking up," K.M.L. Chabbra, executive director of the Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT), told Reuters.
"This will help keep our refineries busy," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
COOIT has estimated the current idle capacity of the oilseeds processing units at 60 percent.
Industry officials and traders said India has so far contracted to import 150,000 tonnes of sunflower oil of which 50,000 tonnes had alreay arrived.
"About 50,000 tonnes of sunflower oil in February and another 50,000 tonnes in March are expected to arrive," said the analyst.
Industry officials said about 200,000 tonnes of edible oil had arrived during the 1996/97 (November-October) season.

"Immediately the supply situation is good but after May, we have to think about more imports when the lean season starts," said G.K. Shah, a former senior official of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd.
"Chinese purchases of oils and oilseeds have come down to an extent during the last 10 days. This might ease their palm olein prices," the analyst said.
He said Malaysian palm olein was currently priced at more than $600 per tonne CIF and imports from Malaysia would pick up once it fell to around $570 per tonne.
"The summer crop estimate will be somewhat clear in another 10 day's time. That will determine the future edible oil imports," he said.
The Agriculture Ministry has set a output target of 9.5 million tonnes of summer oilseeds.

India harvests two oilseed crops annually, with the bulk of its output from the winter crop. The winter crop is sown in July and harvest starts from October. The summer crop harvest starts from March.
Traders said sunflower (crude) was quoted at around 26,500 ($740) rupees compared to 27,000 rupees last week.
Traders said groundnut oil was currently quoted at around 34,000 rupees per tonne, the same as last week. Palm olein was also quoted at around 28,000 rupees, unchanged from last week.
-- Sambit Mohanty, New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024 ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
